clue.text: Quickly assemble for practice

definitions.meaning: to knock something up is to put it together in a hurry
in tennis a ... is the warm-up rally before a match

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday British usage: a hurried construction job, and the pre-match warm-up hit in racket sports.

clue.text: Cheap to demolish

definitions.meaning: to knock a building down is to flatten it

explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective describes bargain prices; the verb phrase means to raze a structure.

clue.text: Told to do a supervisory job abroad

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the phrase's synonym is heard rather than read

parts.note: to oversee is to supervise work

explanation.surface: Someone is informed they will be managing staff in a foreign posting.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversea is an adverb meaning in or to foreign lands across the water.

clue.text: Playful friends embrace game half-heartedly

indicators.note: friends who embrace something hold it inside their arms, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: kith, as in kith and kin, means friends and acquaintances

indicators.note: the heart of the game's name is its pair of middle letters, and half of that pair is dropped

parts.note: tennis is a racket game

explanation.surface: Fun-loving companions throw themselves into a sport without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Kith survives mainly in the phrase kith and kin. The heart of the game is its central pair of letters, and only half of that pair goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittenish describes frisky, playful behaviour like a young cat's.

clue.text: By the sound of it, full of understanding

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is to be judged by how it is heard when spoken

parts.note: packed means crammed full

explanation.surface: Something seems to be brimming with comprehension when you listen to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is an agreement, and an understanding between parties is the same thing.

clue.text: Lines up charter business in advance

indicators.note: the business abbreviation goes ahead of the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
taken as written
to charter a boat is to let or hire it

explanation.surface: Someone queues up to hire a vessel for a company ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read up, charter, business, but 'in advance' puts CO first.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of rhyming verse lines.

clue.text: Scene of historic murder revealed by a current review

indicators.note: to review something is to go over it again, here working the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Fresh evidence about a famous killing comes to light in a topical news survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' is a link. Thomas Becket was murdered in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop Thomas Becket was killed in that Kent cathedral city in 1170, the most famous killing in English church history.

clue.text: It's up to theory, oddly, to state absolute

indicators.note: oddly says to keep the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the phrase

explanation.surface: A philosopher declares that stating a truth with certainty depends on theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to state' is a second definition the setter adds: to utter is to state. 'It's' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter is an intensifying adjective meaning complete or total, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Generous with money after one's left African country

indicators.note: the money abbreviation is placed after the shortened country
one having left the country's name means that letter goes out of it

parts.note: Liberia is a West African republic
one is I as a Roman numeral
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone becomes free with cash once a person has departed from an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with money' reads as part of the definition (liberal with money), but 'with' is a link and 'money' supplies the pound abbreviation, from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means open-handed, giving freely, as in a liberal helping.

clue.text: Where drivers go on Thursday in force

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: in golf a driver hits the ball from the tee

explanation.surface: Motorists head somewhere at the end of the week in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests motorists, but these are golf clubs. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A law with teeth has real power to enforce itself, so teeth means effective strength.

clue.text: Public upset when urn is disposed of

indicators.note: something disposed of is thrown away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to overturn something is to upset or tip it over
taken as written

explanation.surface: Funeral guests are distressed when a burial vessel is thrown away in front of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, in plain view rather than secretly.

clue.text: Policeman makes criminal secure

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
stable means firm and secure

explanation.surface: An officer makes sure a wrongdoer is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest-ranking police officer in Britain.

clue.text: Smack with hesitation on face

parts.note: a smacker is slang for a kiss, and a smack on the lips is a kiss
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone pauses before slapping another person across the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' suggests a slap; here it is a loud kiss. 'with' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Kisser is slang for the mouth or face.

clue.text: One of four rulers starts to totally eclipse the remaining 3

indicators.note: the starts of the next words are their opening letters

parts.note: 3 points to the answer of 3 down, which means playful, and arch is a synonym meaning roguish or playful

explanation.surface: A monarch begins to outshine the rest of the trio entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The '3' is a cross-reference to 3 down, whose answer means playful, giving ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrarch governed one quarter of a province in the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Not worth considering without trial

definitions.meaning: a proposal ruled ... is dismissed as unworthy of attention
a case settled ... is resolved before any hearing

explanation.definitionFit: Both are legal idioms: one for dismissing an idea, one for settling a dispute privately.

clue.text: Permit a front page to show animals

parts.note: to OK something is to permit it
the front page is page one, written P (page) and I (Roman one)

explanation.surface: Someone allows a newspaper's lead page to feature wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'animals' still fits, since the plural of this animal can be the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of central Africa related to the giraffe; its plural can stay unchanged.

clue.text: Without check. I'd blunder somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to making a mistake unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbridled means unrestrained, like a horse with no bridle to hold it back.

clue.text: Awkwardly placed, like Sidney Carton, finally

definitions.meaning: a British idiom for being in trouble or a fix
Sidney Carton in A Tale of Two Cities is taken to the guillotine in a tumbril at the end

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in difficulties; Dickens's hero literally rides in the condemned cart to his execution.

clue.text: Fiddle is tried on to confuse

indicators.note: to fiddle with something is to tamper with it, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A violin is tested to see whether it baffles anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a noun, the violin, but it is the anagram signal. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorient someone is to make them lose their bearings, bewildering them.

clue.text: TV character not half bright enough, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
taking away half of the word leaves only its first half here

explanation.surface: Someone on television is regrettably not quite clever enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps BRI from BRIGHT; 'unfortunately' rearranges BRI plus ENOUGH. Neighbours is an Australian TV soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Every character in the long-running Australian soap Neighbours is, by its title, a person living next door.

clue.text: Confiscate £1,000,000

parts.note: a million pounds is read as one M pound: I for one, M for million, then the pound sign

explanation.surface: Authorities seize a fortune of a million.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints £1,000,000. One million pounds is I (one) + M (million) + POUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound goods is to seize them by legal authority.

clue.text: Pressure failing to open lock

indicators.note: a word failing to open has lost its first letter

parts.note: stress is pressure or strain

explanation.surface: Insufficient force means a door lock will not open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: Career English doctor is first to take up

indicators.note: the English and doctor pieces come first, ahead of the career synonym

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
to career is to race along

explanation.surface: An English physician's profession comes first when deciding what to pursue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a profession; it is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or cause is to adopt it eagerly.

clue.text: Lower classes want music with upper-class beat

parts.note: pop is popular music
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, as in U and non-U
to lace someone is to thrash or beat them

explanation.surface: Ordinary people want a song with a posh rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' suggests rhythm in a musical surface; it means thrash. 'want' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the common people, the general mass as opposed to the elite.

clue.text: Problem concerning bribe coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

explanation.surface: A difficulty arises regarding a backhander that is on the agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the whole of RE + SOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question or tricky problem.

clue.text: Woman worked as daily

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A woman was employed as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaning woman who comes in each day. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a woman's given name.

clue.text: See the writer, given honour by sovereign, strut

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themself as me
MBE, ... of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
R, for Rex or Regina, stands for the reigning monarch

explanation.surface: Look at the author swaggering, decorated by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strut' looks like a verb meaning swagger, but it is a structural bar. 'See' and 'given ... by' place the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering a member is a structural component such as a beam or brace.

clue.text: Mum goes to work in store

parts.note: mum as in keep mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Mother heads off to a job in a retail outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is a mother on the surface, but here it means quiet. 'goes to' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop is a retail store.

clue.text: Alaskan old-timer makes off with money

parts.note: milk that is off has gone sour
dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A veteran of the north steals some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes off with' suggests theft; 'off' is SOUR and 'makes', 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourdough was the name for a veteran prospector in Alaska or the Yukon, after the starter dough they carried.

clue.text: Feast with mouth open

explanation.definitionFit: Two different words share the spelling: a communal meal of early Christians, and an adjective for open-mouthed astonishment.

clue.text: Happy medium — nothing lost by worker

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: radio is a broadcasting medium
O looks like zero, nothing
the ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A balanced, contented state is reached when nothing is wasted by an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy medium' reads as one phrase; it splits into definition and wordplay. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant describes someone glowing with joy.

clue.text: When neither side wins in long case

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
a tie is a match with no winner

explanation.surface: A drawn contest makes a legal dispute drag on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a lawsuit; it is a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's case is a person under treatment.
